reconciliation_result.minimum_safe_requirement_under_this_fixt: The claim-incarnation fence must contain at least one authority-backed component that cannot be reused across reset/fork incarnations, or an equivalent globally monotonic/non-repeating incarnation identity. Merely naming an epoch is insufficient if the epoch identifier can repeat.
reconciliation_result.safe_comparison_rule: If all visible fence fields can repeat, equality cannot prove same-incarnation identity. Treat the record as ambiguous and keep stale retries non-mutating unless non-reuse or a stronger atomic incarnation fence is proven.

observations: Two semantically distinct claim incarnations can be made visibly identical when epoch_id, generation and token are all reusable.
Therefore composite {epoch_id, generation, token} does not solve ABA-style stale attribution unless at least one component has a trustworthy non-reuse property across resets/forks.
Under this fixture the safe action is no stale mutation and no historical-success attribution from equality alone.
inference: Within this exact deterministic model, the previous epoch-scoped composite fence is safe only if epoch identity is itself non-reusable, or if another authority-backed incarnation component supplies equivalent non-reuse/global monotonicity. This fixture does not prove any concrete allowed transport can create that fence atomically, durably couple it to mutation, exclude forks, or guarantee liveness.
